articles.title: European football: Mbappé eases Real Madrid past Valencia to move joint top
articles.summary: Valverde opens scoring in 3-0 victory for Real Madrid. Bayern beat Mainz but Neuer’s record-breaking day turns sour. Kylian Mbappé scored for the seventh match running as Real Madrid pulled provisionally level on points with La Liga leaders Barcelona after a 3-0 win at 10-man Valencia on Saturday.
body: Reigning champions Barça visit Atlético Madrid, third, on Sunday, aiming to move back clear of the chasing pack. José Mourinho’s Madrid largely dominated at Mestalla stadium as they secured an eighth win in a row across all competitions.

Federico Valverde and Arda Guler’s first-half goals put Madrid in the driving seat and Mbappé added a third in the second half, bursting onto a dangerous pass by Guler to dart past Stole Dimitrievski and squeeze home his 13th league goal of the campaign.

Bayern Munich secured a 2-1 victory over Mainz in the Bundesliga on Saturday but the form ⁠of goalkeeper Manuel Neuer will again be in the spotlight after another error almost produced an equaliser for the home side ⁠in the first ⁠half.

Neuer became Bayern’s ​oldest player at 40 years, 225 days, overtaking Bernd Dreher, but was forced off with a recurrence of a foot injury ⁠that had kept him out of recent matches, replaced before half-time by Jonas Urbig.

articles.title: Scottish roundup: Naderi fires Rangers past St Mirren to keep pressure on Celtic
articles.summary: Rangers win 2-0 to go one point off top spot. Aberdeen slump to 4-0 defeat against Hibernian. Rangers banished their recent away day blues with a solid 2-0 win at St Mirren.
body: Draws against Dundee and Hearts in their last two Scottish Premiership games away from Ibrox had blemished their title challenge, but Derek McInnes’s side were determined to leave Paisley without a mark on them.

The in-form striker Ryan Naderi scored with a soft penalty after 18 minutes before the returning skipper, Dan Neil, added a second just after the hour mark with a deflected strike to extend Rangers’ unbeaten run in all competitions to 12 games.

Rangers moved to within one point of the leaders, Celtic, having played the same number of fixtures, albeit Celtic can restore their four-point lead against Kilmarnock at home on Sunday before the the international break gives them another breather.
The Aberdeen manager Stephen Robinson insists he will face the challenge head on as his side go into the international break in real trouble at the wrong end of the table.

articles.title: Truro City game at Folkestone called off after Yassine En-Neyah has medical emergency in warm-up
articles.summary: National League South match postponed. Player now ‘stable and chatting’ in hospital. Truro’s National League South game at Folkestone Invicta was called off after the visitors’ midfielder Yassine En-Neyah had a medical emergency and was taken to hospital.
body: The 26-year-old was transported to the William Harvey Hospital in Ashford for treatment but was responsive on Saturday night, according to an update from the Cornwall club.
“He is stable, sitting up and chatting, but will remain in hospital overnight under observation,” a Truro City statement read.
“The club would like to place on record its thanks to Truro City’s medical staff, their counterparts at Folkestone Invicta, along with all club personnel from the home club.
“Both the National League and Football Association have also offered their help and support. There have also been many well wishes from Truro City fans and the wider football community too.”

articles.title: Enzo Maresca rues Manchester City’s lack of desire after defeat at Nottingham Forest
articles.summary: ‘You need desire and intensity … we didn’t match them’ City have now lost three successive league matches. Enzo Maresca blamed his side’s lack of desire and the way they were outgunned in duels for a third successive Premier League defeat.
body: Jair Cunha dispossessed Josko Gvardiol to score the opener, then Liam Delap struck twice with muscular surges on the break as Forest won their first home league game since April. “Today I think [the problem] has been general,” said Maresca. “It’s not about one player. In the first half we lost all the duels, all the contacts. Against this team, that is fighting relegation, if you don’t match them … it’s something we need to understand. In this kind of game, if you’re not able to win duels and second balls like in the first half, you struggle.

“You need desire and intensity to win second balls and duels. You require intensity or you struggle and we didn’t match their intensity. The second and third goals are copy and paste, lost duels first in the middle of pitch then at the edge of the box.”
points: ‘You need desire and intensity … we didn’t match them’ City have now lost three successive league matches.

articles.title: 'Bruno's as good as ever' - Carrick backs Man Utd captain
articles.summary: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick says captain Bruno Fernandes' commitment to the club is "undoubted" and the midfielder is "as good as ever".
body: Fernandes was left on the bench for October's home defeat by Bournemouth after criticising Carrick and his coaching staff in the wake of the 4-1 Champions League hammering in Como.
Restored to the team for the Premier League defeat by Chelsea a week later, Fernandes scored a retaken penalty to spark his side's stunning second-half comeback against Roma on Tuesday.
Portugal international Fernandes said afterwards there had been "a lot of lies" reported about his relationship with Carrick.
The 32-year-old rejected the notion there had been "clear-the-air talks" between the pair - something which had been confirmed by club sources.

articles.title: 'Very disappointed' Russell says Mercedes error cost him Sao Paulo GP pole
articles.summary: George Russell said he was "really disappointed" as he insisted a "misjudgement" by his Mercedes team had cost him pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
body: Russell drove impressively throughout a hugely-challenging wet qualifying session at Interlagos but ultimately missed out on pole position by two tenths to McLaren's Lando Norris.
The Mercedes driver had led Norris by four tenths of a second after their first runs in Q3, but was then told to abort his second run when he was being held up by the Williams of Alex Albon.

Mercedes thought that Russell would have time to complete another push lap, but the rain intensified moments later and prevented anyone from going faster for the seven minutes of the session that remained.

Russell reacted with fury over team radio, questioning the instruction for him to abort and insisting that regardless of the time he was losing behind Albon, he would have been able to better Norris' time.

articles.title: 'We squashed it' - Hamilton reveals details of talks with Leclerc after fall out
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton says he and Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc have "squashed" their incident at the Mexico City Grand Prix after holding talks in Brazil.
body: Hamilton, Leclerc and team principal Frederic Vasseur held talks on Thursday night to discuss the incident which saw Max Verstappen take advantage of the opening lap Ferrari squabble last Sunday to win the race.
Hamilton has subsequently been critical of Leclerc in interviews and said that discussions were required to more clearly define their rules of combat to avoid costly repeats in future.
Hamilton will start at the back of the grid for Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix due to a power unit change and spoke to the media for the first time on Saturday since his talks with Leclerc.
"Fred hasn't cleared the air in a sense. Me and Charles sat and spoke and we squashed it, and we're moving on," he told Sky Sports F1.

articles.summary: Rangers moved one point behind Scottish Premiership leaders Celtic thanks to goals from Ryan Naderi and Dan Neil in a 2-0 win over St Mirren.
body: Draws against Dundee and Hearts in their last two Premiership games away from Ibrox had blemished the Gers' focused title challenge, but Derek McInnes's side were determined to leave The Marbill Coaches Stadium without a mark on them.
In-form striker Ryan Naderi scored a penalty after 18 minutes after James Penrice was fouled - a decision Sky Sports' co-commentator James McFadden called "softer than soft".
Dan Neil added a second just after the hour mark with a deflected strike to extend the Light Blues' unbeaten run in all competitions to 12 games.

Rangers moved to within one point of leaders Celtic having played the same number of fixtures, albeit the Hoops can can restore their four-point lead against Kilmarnock at Celtic Park on Sunday before the international break gives the league another breather.

articles.title: 'A different Noni?' Madueke finding a new level for Arsenal
articles.summary: Noni Madueke lay sprawled on the turf, head in his hands, following his one-on-one miss late in Arsenal's 1-0 victory over Hull. His frustration continued to show even after the final whistle.
body: The winger's reaction showed the standards this "different Noni", to quote Mikel Arteta, is setting himself as he strives to reach another level. Bukayo Saka's injury was a significant setback to Arsenal. Madueke has made it his mission to soften the blow.

So far, he has filled in impressively. Arteta understood his demeanour after the game. "He knew he had three clear chances to score," he said, always demanding more. But there was also an acknowledgement of his crucial role in Martin Odegaard's goal.

Madueke's shot forced the Konstantinos Tzolakis save from which his captain scored. It was just one of many dangerous moments. His total of 13 touches in the opposition box was the most by an Arsenal in any Premier League game this season.

Madueke also hit his highest totals in a game this term for shots and chances created, with a combined eight, and successful dribbles, with five. This was not a vintage attacking display from Arsenal but almost everything positive came through him.

articles.title: Masuk sweeps Brookfield to claim first SWC girls volleyball title in program history
articles.summary: Mia Tyler had 32 assists, four digs, three kills and two aces as Masuk defeated Brookfield 3-0 to win its first South-West Conference girls volleyball championship Thursday night at Weston High. Tyler earned tournament Most Valuable Player honors. The set scores were 25-18, 25-14, 25-18.
body: Masuk had been 0-for-4 in SWC girls volleyball championship matches, losing to Bunnell in 2004 and Joel Barlow in 2019, 2020 and last season.
As the No. 1 seed in the conference tournament, the Panthers (20-2) beat No. 8 New Milford 3-1 in the quarterfinals before sweeping No. 4 Joel Barlow 3-0 in the semifinals.
Brookfield (12-11), the No. 7 seed, upset No. 2 Newtown 3-2 in the quarterfinals and No. 3 Weston 3-2 in the semifinals.
Addison Scott had 23 kills, seven digs and three assists for Masuk, while Grace Morrow added 15 digs and two kills.

articles.title: Pietra Tordin and Sophia Wilson fuel Portland Thorns attack ahead of NWSL playoff clash with Washington Spirit
articles.summary: After losing Olivia Moultrie to injury, Portland found an explosive dynamic duo capable of pulling off a quarterfinal upset against Washington's vulnerable defense
body: Sophia Wilson is back with a vengeance. After missing the 2025 season, she's finished the regular season with the third-most goals in the league, behind only Ashley Sanchez and Barbara Banda. Those 15 goals are an impressive number as she and the Thorns enter the NWSL playoffs, where they'll travel to face the Washington Spirit. But while Wilson and Trinity Rodman will be the headliners of the match, how Portland's attack ticks over is what'll be critical as they try to stop the Spirit from making a run to their third consecutive appearance in the NWSL final in Sunday's quarterfinal matchup.
